title: Sample 14-9: Mixed Prose and Verse Stage Directions

illustrates.quote: Mixed Prose and Verse Plays. Dialogue. Use the appropriate format for the type of dialogue, i.e., 1-3 margins for the prose sections and 1-5, 3-5 margins for the verse sections. Stage Directions. Use 7-7 margins for stage directions or cues. Follow print for use of enclosure symbols.

blocks.speaker: Ophelia:
blocks.text: Ophelia: I hope all will be well. We must be patient: but I cannot choose but weep, to think they should lay him i' the cold ground. My brother shall know of it: and so I thank you for your good counsel. Come, my coach! Good night, ladies; good night, sweet ladies; good night, good night.

blocks.speaker: King:
blocks.text: King: Follow her close; give her good watch,
O, this is the poison of deep grief; it springs
All from her father’s death. O Gertrude, Gertrude,
When sorrows come, they come not single spies

print.notes: King's own speech begins in PROSE (1-3, no verse) and, after a stage direction interrupts it, continues in VERSE with no speaker name repeated — confirmed directly against the given braille's own margins: the verse portion sits at cell 3/5 (3-5, the 'additional line by the same speaker' margin, 14.6.1b) throughout, never at cell 1/5 (a fresh verse 'first line'), so it is modelled as three level-1 verse blocks continuing the same speech, not a new speech. Ophelia's own elided “i' the” keeps a plain (straight) apostrophe — confirmed by forward translation: a curly right-single-quote apostrophe there translates to a DIFFERENT symbol (a French/foreign-language single-quote indicator) that the given braille does not have.
print.printFeatures: A prose speech, a bracketed stage direction, a second prose speech, a second stage direction, then three lines of verse continuing the second speaker's own turn.
